No pre-commit hooks either — `lint` exists only as a manual script. That confirms the picture. Here's the retro, worst problem first.

## 1. (Critical) Hand-edited generated file — this is the bug that shipped

`src/db/generated-types.ts:1` is stamped `// AUTO-GENERATED. Do not edit.` and is rebuilt from `src/db/schema.ts` by `scripts/gen-types.ts` (`pnpm db:generate`). The agent added `currency: string` straight into the generated file and never touched `schema.ts` (which, confirmed by reading it, has no `currency` on `refunds` at all). The next regeneration silently drops the hand-added field — exactly the "currency field disappeared" report, and almost certainly why CI went red on `main` afterward.

CLAUDE.md already has the rule ("Never commit generated files by hand") but nothing tells the agent *where the real source of truth is* or *what happens if you ignore it*.

- **`CLAUDE.md`** — under "Where things are," add a pointer: `DB shape changes: edit src/db/schema.ts, then run pnpm db:generate. Hand-edits to src/db/generated-types.ts are silently overwritten.` This is a one-line navigation pointer that would have prevented the entire incident.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — add a drift-check step: `pnpm db:generate && git diff --exit-code src/db/generated-types.ts`. This turns "don't hand-edit generated files" from a prose rule into something CI actually enforces, catching this class of bug regardless of whether any agent reads CLAUDE.md carefully.

## 2. (Critical) Lint isn't wired into CI, and the lint config can't even parse this codebase's TypeScript

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` only runs `typecheck` and `test` — `pnpm lint` is never invoked, and there's no pre-commit hook either. On top of that, `eslint.config.js` only loads `@eslint/js` (plain JS rules); `package.json` has no `typescript-eslint` dependency at all, so even run manually, ESLint has no TS parser and can't understand this codebase's type annotations. There is currently no automated check in this repo that could ever catch a mechanical rule violation.

This is why three separate CLAUDE.md rules were broken in one diff with nothing catching them:
- `never use any` → `orderRepo.ts` added `findRefund` returning `any`
- `never import from src/internal/* outside the module that owns it` → `router.ts:2` imports `query` from `../internal/pg-driver.js` directly
- `every exported function that can fail returns Result<T,E>` → `orderRepo.findOrder`/`findRefund` and `router.route` all return raw/nullable/`any` types instead

Fix:
- **`package.json`** — add `typescript-eslint` (and `@typescript-eslint/parser`) as a devDependency.
- **`eslint.config.js`** — use `typescript-eslint`'s recommended config, enable `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` (catches finding #2's `any`), and add a `no-restricted-imports` rule blocking `**/internal/*` from outside `src/db` (catches the import-boundary breach). These are exactly the "mechanical, fixed-pattern" violations this skill's guidance says belong in a linter, not in prose.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — add a `- run: pnpm lint` step so it actually runs.

## 3. (High) The reviewer only checks `CODING_STANDARDS.md`, and that file doesn't mention any of CLAUDE.md's correctness-critical rules

The reviewer transcript says "Reviewed the diff against CODING_STANDARDS.md" and approved despite the `any`, the import breach, and the missing `Result<T,E>` wrapping. `CODING_STANDARDS.md` only covers judgment calls (error-message voice, abstraction threshold, export style) — it has zero mention of `any`, import boundaries, or the `Result<T,E>` contract, so the reviewer had no instruction to look for them.

The `any` and import-boundary cases are now covered mechanically by finding #2's lint rules, which is the right fix for those (per this skill's guidance: mechanical → deterministic check, not reviewer prose). But `Result<T,E>` adoption isn't cleanly lintable without a custom rule, and right now the reviewer isn't even told it's in scope.

- **`CODING_STANDARDS.md`** — add a line telling the reviewer to check that exported functions which can fail return `Result<T, E>` rather than throwing/returning null/any, since that's a correctness contract, not just style, and nothing else will catch it once the lint rules above absorb the other two violations.

## 4. (Medium) `CODING_STANDARDS.md` directly contradicts `CLAUDE.md` on exports

`CLAUDE.md:16`: "Prefer named exports over default exports." `CODING_STANDARDS.md:9`: "Prefer default exports for single-export modules." These are flatly opposed, so implementation and review are working from different rules.

- **`CODING_STANDARDS.md`** — delete the "Prefer default exports" line, or if there's a genuine judgment-call exception intended (e.g., single-export CLI entry points), rewrite it to say so explicitly and reconcile it with CLAUDE.md's wording rather than contradicting it outright.

## 5. (Medium) `CLAUDE.md` points at a script that doesn't exist

`CLAUDE.md:36`: "Run `pnpm test:unit` before every commit." `package.json` has no `test:unit` script, only `test`. The agent hit `ERR_PNPM_NO_SCRIPT` and had to guess the right command — a wasted tool call from steering-file drift.

- **`CLAUDE.md`** — change line 36 to `pnpm test`.

## 6. (Medium) The mandatory "run status-report first" step is a no-op that costs real context

`CLAUDE.md:7-8` requires running `pnpm status-report` before *any* task. It dumped 422 lines of per-module deploy/queue-depth boilerplate with nothing relevant to a refunds/currency task, and the transcript notes none of it was used. This is pure context load paid on every single task regardless of relevance.

- **`CLAUDE.md`** — drop the blanket "before starting any task" instruction, or narrow it to when it's actually useful (e.g., "when investigating cross-service incidents, check `pnpm status-report`"). If nothing in this repo's workflow ever actually consumes `docs/status-dump.txt`, consider removing the step entirely.

## 7. (Low) `dev` script suppresses all output, so the agent can never verify runtime behavior

`package.json`: `"dev": "tsx watch src/cli/serve.ts > /dev/null 2>&1"`. The transcript shows the agent starting the dev server to confirm the endpoint, waiting, retrying twice, and giving up because no log line was ever visible — the script redirects everything to `/dev/null` by construction.

- **`package.json`** — remove the `> /dev/null 2>&1` redirect (or redirect to a log file the agent can `Read`/`tail`) so runtime verification is actually possible instead of structurally blocked.
